title: How fast can a thing become something else?

data.source: Mandelstam and Tamm (1945); Margolus and Levitin (1998); Anandan and Aharonov (1990). Computed for a qubit and for three-level systems.

prediction: For a qubit with equal weights the CRR half-turn, the moment of orthogonality and both quantum speed limits are the same time, pi; for three equally weighted levels the state is orthogonal at 2.0944 but the half-turn comes at 3.1416, where the overlap is still 1/3.
baseline: The Mandelstam-Tamm bound (1945) and the Margolus-Levitin bound (1998) on the time to reach an orthogonal state.
why: For the evenly weighted qubit the cut is the orthogonalisation time and equals the Mandelstam-Tamm bound, because that path is a geodesic and the bound is then an equality: CRR restates it. For three levels the cut came a third of a turn after orthogonality; for a tilted qubit orthogonality never came; for unevenly spaced levels the path never closed exactly, though it came back nearer than I had predicted. Phoenix files the quantum mapping as SPARK and says an equivalence to known quantum Fisher geometry REDUCES; this check agrees and shows where the equivalence stops.
